title: Session expired
summary: What the app does when the homeserver stops taking an account's token (bipe-chat/bipe#204, ADR 0057). A device-first account has no password to type: the app signs in again with the hidden password, and asks only for the PIN when that is not possible.

userId.description: The account whose token the server refused. Never shown.

phase.description: signingIn: the quiet sign-in with the hidden password runs; nothing shows. needsPin: recovery-pin for this account, titled bipe_soft_logout_title. removed: another device signed this phone out; the account left the phone.

isSoftLogout.description: ClientDelegate.didReceiveAuthError. true: the token expired and the device still exists. false: the device was signed out on the server.

authError.effect: isSoftLogout true: stops the sync, builds a client on the same store and runs Client.login with the hidden password and the same device ID, so keys and history stay; saves the new session and starts the sync. No hidden password, or the server refuses it: phase needsPin. isSoftLogout false: runs sign-out with alreadyLoggedOut (spec sign-out signOut, the server step is already done) and shows bipe_soft_logout_removed once.

enterPin.effect: In needsPin: recovery-pin with factor token for the synced recovery token of this account. A good PIN signs the account in again (recovery-pin submit). Without a synced token for it: recovery-start.

later.effect: Closes the PIN screen. The account stays on the phone without a session; the next foreground or app start asks again.

notes: The person never types a password and never sees a homeserver name or a Matrix ID (ADR 0057). No English-only text on this path.
A network error during the quiet sign-in keeps phase signingIn and tries again on the next foreground. It never deletes the hidden password, the saved session or the SDK store.

needsPin removes only the saved SDK session of the account, whose token the server refused, so recovery-start can offer the account's synced token. The hidden password and the store stay until a sign-in replaces them.
A device that another device signed out (linked-devices signOut) must not sign in again by itself: that is how a person locks out a lost phone. Hence removed, never a quiet sign-in.
bipe_soft_logout_body and bipe_soft_logout_removed take the account's display name.
With several accounts on the phone (ADR 0086), only the account whose token failed is affected; the others keep working.

The recovery-start row beta (bipe_recovery_beta, e-mail and password) shows in every build, release included (MZ, 26 Oct 2026): App Review signs in with the demo account through it (App Review guideline 2.1). After that sign-in the app moves the account to device-first, which sets a new password; the API refuses the move while the account has no PIN (pin_not_set), so the demo account must stay without a PIN.
